# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 106 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 106 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_106_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 23

**1** I saw the tower and the lord of the tower, and those who were building it, greatly glorifying the Lord. **2** I asked the shepherd who stood beside me, "Who is this lord of the tower?" "It is the Son of God," he answered. **3** "And these six men and the virgins with them?" "These are the holy angels of the Lord, and the virgins are the holy spirits." **4** "And the young men building the tower?" "These also are holy angels of the Lord, but the six are set over them. All who build the tower shall enter the kingdom of God. **5** But the others who brought stones shall also enter the kingdom, if they walk in truth." **6** "And those who brought stones but could not fit them in — who are they?" **7** "These had believed but departed on account of their double-mindedness; they were not inserted into the building because they were double-minded and full of malice. **8** They shall be excluded from the kingdom of God." **9** "And the round stones that fit nowhere — who are they?" **10** "These also are those who have believed," he said, "but possess great wealth in this world; when affliction comes, because of their riches and their business they deny the Lord." **11** I asked him, "When then shall they be fit for the building of the tower?" **12** "When," he said, "the riches that have ensnared their souls have been cut away from them — then they shall be useful to the Lord. **13** Just as a round stone can only become square when something is cut away and removed from it, so those who are wealthy can only become useful to God when their riches are cut away from them. **14** Learn this from yourself: when you were wealthy you were useless; but now you are useful and profitable for life."

---

*LOGOS: the double-mindedness and full malice of the stone-bringers who couldn't fit is distinct from double-mindedness alone — it is the combination that excludes.*
